questions: Did these movements begin suddenly, within hours or a few days?
Did they begin after starting, stopping, or changing a medication?
Have you taken antipsychotic medicines, such as haloperidol, risperidone, or quetiapine?
Have you taken metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, or another medicine for nausea?
Have you used cocaine, amphetamines, or other stimulant drugs recently?
Do the movements continue while you are asleep?
Are your legs, face, tongue, or trunk also affected?
Have you had episodes of loss of awareness or seizures?
Have you developed weakness, numbness, difficulty speaking, or difficulty walking?
Have you had fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, or a recent infection?
Have you had a recent head injury or stroke?
Have you ever had similar movements before?
Does anyone in your biological family have involuntary movements, dementia, or a diagnosis of Huntington disease?
Have you noticed recent changes in memory, judgment, mood, or behavior?
Have you had liver disease, jaundice, or unexplained abdominal symptoms?
Have you had new psychiatric symptoms, joint pain, or a rash?
Do you have diabetes or kidney disease?
Are you pregnant or could you be pregnant?
Are the movements less noticeable when you deliberately hold your arms still?
Have the movements been progressively worsening over weeks or months?
